items.headline: Overview
items.summary: Policy Plus is a Windows desktop editor for Group Policy settings, used by administrators and power users.

items.headline: Reading policy definitions

items.headline: Failed load of policy templates leaves the workspace…
items.summary: Staged items survive and make later loads fail, partly filled lists make retries fail on duplicate names, and a download reloads after clearing the workspace

items.headline: Applying a policy file's held changes…
items.summary: Only forgetting old values is limited to policy branches, so a crafted policy file, a different route from a REG import

items.headline: Applying a policy
items.summary: A failure, such as a drop-down with no choice, leaves the policy empty or half set and reports little.

items.headline: Comment loading and saving failures are hidden
items.summary: An unreadable comment file silently disables comments for that source, a failed save is dropped so typed comments are lost

items.headline: Enabling a policy with a list option…
items.summary: The list stays empty until the list editor is used or the source holds one, and nothing checks it.

items.headline: For an administrator
Importing a REG file applies it key…
items.summary: A failure leaves earlier changes in place and the person sees only a general failure message.

items.headline: Importing a REG file applies it to whichever…
items.summary: The branch limit exists only when a REG file is the target, so an import can write, delete or clear keys outside the policy branches.

items.headline: Policy files and REG files are saved…
items.summary: A failure partway leaves a truncated or damaged file, with no copy of the old one.

items.headline: Policy template and comment XML files are read…
items.summary: The folders or domain share they come from may be writable by others, and whether external entities resolve depends on the framework default.

items.headline: Results of requesting Windows privileges and loading…
items.summary: The person learns a source cannot be saved, or silently gets an empty read-only source, never why.

items.headline: Saving a local or per-user policy writes…
items.summary: A failure on the second step, or a malformed version line that truncates the version file, leaves new settings with an old or damaged version

items.headline: Saving reports its result poorly
items.summary: One handler covers both sources without saying which failed, success is shown even when nothing was writable

items.headline: Saving writes the computer source first…
items.summary: If the user save fails, the computer policies are already on disk

items.headline: Template and comment XML files
items.summary: Whether those resolve rests on the framework default, which the code does not settle.

items.headline: Text typed by the person
items.summary: Path characters redirect where policy and version files are created or which folder is searched for definition text, using the person's own rights.

items.headline: Download accepts what it is given without checks
items.summary: For an administrator the files written also get their access rules reset.

items.headline: Download destination is free text and never checked…
items.summary: A wrong existing folder typed or browsed to, which needs an administrator to change the default

items.headline: Downloaded Microsoft template package is run through…
items.summary: The tool processes the package before anything is verified, so a compromised channel or address delivers altered files for the template folder.

items.headline: Microsoft template package is unpacked with no hash…
items.summary: The address is a fixed Microsoft link, which limits exposure to a compromised source or channel.

items.headline: Name of a value added in the raw…
items.summary: An empty name hides the key's marker, and names

items.headline: Program allows TLS 1.0 and 1.1 as well…
items.summary: A server or on-path party forcing an old protocol would be accepted. The download address is fixed HTTPS.

items.headline: Template download deletes each existing file
items.summary: A failure midway leaves the destination partly replaced, and the scratch folder with the downloaded package stays in the person's local data.

items.headline: Template download, run as administrator
items.summary: This happens to the system definitions folder even on the default path, not only when another folder is typed.

items.headline: Template download, when run as administrator
items.summary: The folder defaults to the standard template folder but is not checked, so a wrong existing folder has its ownership and permissions changed.

items.headline: Unsaved policy changes are lost without warning…
items.summary: Opening other sources or exiting closes them with no prompt. Registry sources apply at once, so lose nothing.

items.headline: Values supplied for a policy's settings
items.summary: Numbers are forced to unsigned 32-bit and text is stored as given, ignoring any minimum, maximum or length in the definition.

items.headline: What the template download moves into the policy…
items.summary: With no check of the package, a tampered or substituted one replaces the installed templates, which the program then loads as trusted definitions.

items.headline: When a download, install or export fails
items.summary: A finished install can be reported as a failure when cleanup fails, leaving the new folder unloaded and unpacked files behind.

items.headline: When rights or a per-user registry file cannot…
items.summary: The person is told a source cannot be modified or saved, never why, and can keep editing an empty in-memory source that is never written.

items.headline: Failure to open or create the saved-settings registry…
items.summary: The program then runs without remembering anything and the person is never told.

items.headline: Typed user identifier is joined into the per-user…
items.summary: It acts only with the person's own rights.

items.headline: Changing or loading policy sources has no error…
items.summary: Sources are replaced one by one, so a failure leaves a mix or an empty workspace with an unhandled error.

items.headline: Each template states the minimum text-file revision it…
items.summary: A template can be paired with text too old for it.

items.headline: Escape in the raw policy editor looks like…
items.summary: Changes cannot be discarded except by not saving afterwards.

items.headline: If the program cannot create its settings key…
items.summary: Remembered-source values are also written one by one, so a failure can leave a mismatched pair.

items.headline: Opening a live registry source tests writing…
items.summary: A failure in between leaves the probe value behind, and the failure is swallowed.

items.headline: Reading a policy file trusts the length stored…
items.summary: A damaged or hostile file can demand huge memory or fail unexplained, and REG files report no line number on error.

items.headline: Several windows raise an unhandled error on ordinary…
items.summary: No program-wide handler is set, so the framework's default error dialog appears.

items.headline: Program permits TLS 1.0 and 1.1 alongside 1.2…
items.summary: A connection uses the best version both ends offer, but a server or on-path party forcing an old version would be accepted.

items.headline: Program targets .NET Framework 4.5.2
items.summary: The readme says newer versions also work and ship with Windows 10 or later, which limits the reach to the declared minimum.

items.headline: Template download uses one fixed address naming…
items.summary: When Microsoft retires it, or a newer release appears, the feature fails until the program is rebuilt.

items.headline: When a download, unpack or move fails
items.summary: The scratch folder is removed only on success, and files already moved into the destination are not rolled back.
